shots.action: Continuous take in the wood-panelled carpentry workshop, bright daylight raking through the large multi-paned windows. Behind the workbench the elderly woman with short white hair, wearing her bright yellow raincoat, raises the hammer and drives the nail home with a firm strike; beside the lathe the young woman in the grey apron keeps working, shavings curling off. In the background the young man in the blue coat stands among the benches, glancing toward the workbench. The raincoated woman sets the hammer down and turns from the nail to face the camera, her breath settling as the daylight holds on the room.
shots.what_changes: The bearded man in the plaid shirt is gone from the workbench, replaced by the elderly woman in the yellow raincoat, and the young man in the blue coat now stands in the workshop; the nail is struck and she turns to face the camera as the framing tightens.

structure.reasoning: The request is a two-role swap over the supplied edit-source clip. <Picture 1> (the elderly woman in the yellow raincoat) is the replacement for the caller-named 'man in the plaid shirt', which is observed in the clip as <Subject 3>, so the map resolves to <Subject 3>. <Picture 2> is the replacement for 'the person on the roof', which is not observed anywhere in the clip (the clip is a wood-panelled workshop with a bearded man and a young woman at the lathe, no roof), so that entry stays empty and the young man in the blue coat must be represented as a newly introduced figure rather than mapped onto an unrelated leftover such as <Subject 4>. Nothing in the request touches speech, music or on-screen lettering, so all three stay unrequested and un-forbidden; the clip's bright natural daylight, cinematic live-action medium, workshop palette, medium-wide framing and tightening camera remain reference-governed, and no observed figure or action outside the two swapped roles is altered. The caller pinned one shot and the full 5167 ms duration, so this is a single continuous take with the edit source's action preserved: driving the nail with the hammer and turning to the camera, now performed by the raincoated elderly woman. The portraits are identity plates on studio backdrops, not frames; the grey studio backdrop, studio lighting and full-body plate presentation are not transplanted into the workshop scene. A measured push-in supports the existing tightening without inventing events.
